newsitem.title: MEXICO: More Mexicans approve of Zedillo than not - poll.
newsitem.headline: More Mexicans approve of Zedillo than not - poll.

text.p: For the first time in nearly two years, more Mexicans approved than disapproved of the way President Ernesto Zedillo was handling his job, a poll showed on Monday.

But while many Mexicans feel Zedillo is honest, few think he is doing a good job on the economy and many feel glum about their own economic prospects, according to the poll in Mexico City's Reforma newspaper.

Some 45 percent of 1,500 people polled nationwide approved of the 44-year-old leader while 42 percent did not. In the previous Reforma poll in September, Zedillo's approval and disapproval levels were even at 46 percent.
The poll has a three percentage point margin of error.

It was the first time since March, 1995, four months after Zedillo took power, that more Mexicans approved of him than did not. His approval ratings fell in mid-1995 after the 1994 peso crash caused a belated recession.

The poll, carried out every three months, showed that many Mexicans were still concerned about the economy. Some 37 percent felt it would worsen next year and just 24 percent thought it would improve.
Forty-eight percent of those polled said Zedillo, a Yale-trained economist, was doing a poor or very poor job managing the economy. Only 15 percent thought he was doing a good or very good job.

Mexico's economy fell 6.2 percent in 1995 and was projected to grow by about four percent this year and around the same amount in 1997. Most Mexicans' real purchasing power remained lower than before Zedillo took office two years ago.
Some 31 percent said his government was honest, while 23 percent said it was not, and just four percent said Zedillo was making progress in rooting out corruption.

Asked which political party they would vote for if presidential elections were held today, 30 percent said Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party, 23 percent favoured the conservative National Action Party and 11 percent liked the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution.
